If you buy this, download BSManager, install some mods, then head on over to Beat Saver and download some high-rated playlists off there. Anything with a rating of 85% or more is guaranteed to be a good playlist. There's loads of good levels on there which should keep you going for a long time. Plus, it's good exercise - you can get fit playing video games. What a time to be alive.

When I pull off a really difficult section, I get a sense of accomplishment that it's kind of hard to describe.  I'm a pretty uncoordinated middle aged guy, and for a brief second, I feel cool, although I imagine if I saw myself without the gear on, I'm sure that I'd disagree.
After 31 years on this planet, I finally found a physical activity that I enjoy doing so much that I actively seek it out multiple times a week instead of forcing myself to do it every two months.

Let me tell you a story.

Once upon a time, there was an out-of-shape guy who lived in a modest flat. He bought a VR headset and started to dive into all kinds of VR games. Elite Dangerous VR, Robo Recall, Audioshield, he played it all. The moment he bought Beat Saber, though, his life began to change forever.

At first, he tried the easier difficulties and found them too dull for his taste. Then he tried the expert difficulty and, though he struggled with them at first, managed to finish every single song in the game with a good score, missing only a few notes. As time went on, he grew slightly bored with the game, as it has only a few tracks included. To alleviate the problem, he decided to invest in a decent speaker system and use it instead of relying on the default headphones that came with his Oculus Rift. It barely helped.

By this time, the guy has lost some weight. He then decided to delve into the wonderful world of modding as he installed a few custom beat maps. Now he can theoretically keep himself entertained for as long as his physical endurance allows.

Soon, short sessions became hours long, and everytime he played he always would end up heavily drenched in sweat. Within days, changing T-shirts regularly is a must, followed by showers. The laundry pile grows bigger by the day, and doing the laundry is a chore he would rather not do. It didn't take him long to start playing the game shirtless, with air conditioning on full blast, which allows him to play for hours on end. Still, he had to take regular showers and toss his shorts to the laundry bin.

Of course, this change warrants a few consequences. In one instance, the guy decided to take a shower after yet another long session, but is stopped by his female flatmate, who proceeded to show him the ridiculously hefty water bill. 

She then whispers, "Wanna shower together?"

So, the moral of the story is: BUY THIS GAME!

My Opinion: Beatsaber is an amazing game. Combines guitar hero and fruit ninja with lightsabers, and I truly believe that anyone who owns a VR headset should own, and experience this game. The base game itself has a good selection of music, and has a pretty wide range of difficulties going from easy, to normal, to hard, then to expert and expert+. Beyond the base game, there is a MASSIVE modding community for Beatsaber (the discord server has over 180k members) and they are all there with the same idea in mind: to make an already great game even better. The number of custom songs that people have made will make you believe that there is no song out there that HASN'T been made into a beatsaver map, not to mention custom sabers, custom character models, custom platforms, and multiplayer (if you can figure out how to get it working).

Negative Reviews: A lot of people leave negative reviews for this game for bad reasons. notably those reasons are due to mods breaking due to the game updated, the devs updating the EULA, and videos and streams getting copyright strikes against them. 
-------- Regarding mods breaking due to game updates, this will occur in any game out there that supports modding even officially. I have a history playing minecraft, world of warcraft, 7 days to die, etc. and any time those games update, the mods "break" simply because of the changes made to the base game, all it takes is for us to be patient to wait for the mod devs to update their mods.
-------- Regarding the EULA changes, the beatsaber devs recently updated their EULA with some pretty scary looking remarks that state that modifying the game in any way is prohibited. This does NOT mean that the devs are "banning" mods, this means that the devs are not officially supporting them, because installing mods that download custom songs can be viewed as a form of piracy, which would not look good for the beatsaber devs.
-------- Regarding videos/streams getting copyright strikes, this was due to a TV show having a segment where they played beatsaber, and specifically a small number of songs from the original soundtrack that are royalty free. Because of this, that TV show's parent company striked these videos/streams wrongfully, and this issue has since then been resolved.

If you've made it this far in the review, thank you for your time. As someone with over a hundred hours in this game and no intentions of slowing down, I look forward to being a continued part of BeatSaber's community.

In 2023, Beat Saber is one of those weird games where I'd give it what I call a "conditional" recommendation - definitely if you mod it, definitely not if you don't. Read on for more info.

Let's talk about the "don't" first - the base offering of the game. One of THE coolest playstyles for a rhythm game involving swinging sabers like you're out of Star Wars, moving your body around to avoid walls and swinging your wrists to avoid bombs, being engrossed in a simplistic but easy on the eye and aesthetically intriguing world. Functionally, the game plays very well and you're going to be burning some calories if you play on Hard+. You get a decent amount (I think around 35?) of songs to play around with, multiplayer functionality, an in-game level editor, a campaign mode and more. The songs are alright at best, annoying at worst. Everyone's taste is different. There's a lot of electronica, some hip-hop-esque music, some rock, and a couple others. Only Angel Voices and Escape stuck with me.

More importantly though, how's the mapping with respect to the music? It's okay if you're playing on Hard or less, but my overall experience in Expert and higher is they don't feel like there's good flow. Like some note placement feels like you have to make an unnatural movement or they trick you to lose your combo. Not all songs are like this, and the more recent free OSTs show they have gotten a bit better with the mapping. The campaign mode seemed neat, and I started on that to get introduced to the game. It starts off easy, challenging you with restrictions or getting a minimum combo/score progressively, but then they have some weird counterintuitive tasks like "swing your arms for 900m" where I was using any free gap between notes to swing my arms ridiculously hoping to hit the 900m goal, or weird stuff like "don't get beyond a 25 combo" in a way to manage your energy levels I guess? I did 100% the campaign, but beyond the first few levels, I can't recommend it unless you really want the achievements.

Lastly, let's talk about how the game stands now in 2023. Plenty more rhythm games have come out since, and pretty much all of them are cheaper than this. BS NEVER goes on sale. They patch the game every so often to add a few DLC songs, which are also not cheap unless you get one of their rotating dlc bundles. At $2 a song, if you buy 15 non-discounted songs, you're basically paying for the game again but for significantly less content. I get it. Licensing isn't cheap, but from what I've read the DLCs are very hit-or-miss with their mapping, and some songs are censored without any way to change that? Ridiculous. If you want to do that to make it age-accessible, fine, but at least give us adults a damn toggle. And yes, I get this pricing practice is kind of standard for a lot of rhythm games (including one I strongly recommend, Synth Riders), but come on. In 2023, there are so many other games that offer a better or unique package. Synth Riders. OhShape. Audio Trip (which got overhauled recently). BoomBox. PowerBeatsVR. All of these games are cheaper, go on sale/have discounts, don't muck up your game with patches that add paid songs no one wants, and to those that care, aren't affiliated with Facebook/"Meta". Do I recommend them all? Personally, no, but your experience may be better than mine. Give em a look, especially Synth Riders. That one is probably the best, unless...

Let's talk about Modded Beat Saber. You know how whenever a VR game topic comes up, Beat Saber is almost always mentioned and regarded as a highlight? The modding community is why. It's a grad-school thesis level of INSANE what driven individuals can do. Custom sabers. Global scoreboard functionality. Making and modding a little avatar character to represent yourself. Adding a clock (no joke, I genuinely believe every VR game should have some kind of toggleable clock). Huge customization to pretty much everything, and of course the CUSTOM SONGS. There are THOUSANDS of custom songs, and thanks to the beatmap voting system you can do with custom music and people caring to refine their work, the custom maps are overall superior to anything the base game has. Caramelldansen is genuinely one of the best maps I've ever played in any rhythm game, and it isn't too hard so with a little practice everyone can experience it! Again, thousands of songs and a plethora of customization options to give yourself the definitive experience, and the modding setup is so easy even I can do it and I'm pretty clumsy with some modding stuff. The additions mods make are what base Beat Saber SHOULD HAVE BECOME, in my opinion, and even though I wrote mostly negative things about the base game, I can't say anything but positive stuff once you get mods setup. Right now I think like 85-90% of my playtime comes from modded BS, and since I 100%d the achievements and don't find myself touching anything from base, this % will just keep rising. Absolute gold standard in VR rhythm gaming.

TL:DR - Mod Beat Saber, and/or get Synth Riders.

As a big fan of Guitar Hero, and as a person interested in music, I was certainly excited when I first saw a gameplay video of this game. I bought the HTC Vive just a few days before Beat Saber was released, and tried a few other games, but as soon as this game was released, playing the Vive has been the same as playing Beat Saber.

The game is really simple. In a good way. I’ve had many friends over, and I just pop the Vive over their head, start the game, and just let them have it. All of them get what they have to do immediately. All of them sound a little anxious, feel a bit ashamed that they miss a block or two, but a couple of seconds later, they’re completely immersed in the game. As soon as the song is over, they quietly ask: “Can I have another go?”.

For me, this game quickly became a huge motivation. I want to be better, I want to hit those global leaderboards. It’s no casual gaming anymore. I’m putting on shorts, prepare a water bottle, and play all out until I’m spent, lying panting on the floor. Even if I don’t hit those leaderboards, at least I’ll be as fit as Arnold Schwarzenegger was in his golden days by the end of the summer. And this is the first time in forever that I’ve been this motivated by a game.

Even though the songs are far from the kind of music that I listen to, I cannot help but walk around having the melodies in my head constantly. Some songs I play because I like the music, others I play because the level is just really fun to play. And some because both of those reasons. In general the music and levels are really well done, and I’m really looking forward to more songs and user-made content. I’m hoping the genres will be a bit more diverse later on, but I’m really impressed with how good these first songs are.

I do have a couple of suggestions to improve the game though:

I would like it if I could practice a certain part of a certain song, much like you could in Guitar Hero, so you can really hone your skills. Now your only chance to practice and study the song is to turn on the “No Energy”-mode and play without the risk of failing the level. If the part you’re having trouble with is 1 minute and 30 seconds in, it’s kind of frustrating to play through the song over and over again and not get a chance to really practice the hard part before you have to restart the song again. So a training-mode, where maybe you could even slow down the speed or something, to really perfect your gameplay, would be awesome. 

The other thing that has been bothering me are the blocks that have no arrow, but a point on them. Everyone who’s tried the game, me included, has tried to stab these blocks the first time they’ve encountered them. It took a couple of tries before I realized that they were a “Swing however you want”-block. I think it would be better if these blocks had no marking at all. That would be more clear as to what you’re supposed to do with them.

Also, I would like to look as cool as I feel when playing. I don’t. I look stupid. Like I’m randomly waving my hands around, uncontrollably. Can you make me look like a jedi master instead? I would appreciate that.

Thanks for one of the best gaming experiences I’ve had in ages!

Beat Saber is a classic arcade rhythm game with the twist of existing in a virtual space and wielding light sabers. This is not the sort of game I envisaged myself playing. I'm an old, overweight, slow and honestly, a lazy gamer who saw YouTube videos of people flailing around and shook her head in bemusement. Yet here I am, doing an impression of a flying chicken as I duck under obstacles and try to hit note after addictive note and going to bed complaining that my arms are sore.

There's something about Beat Saber that is honestly just fun. It gets you moving even if you hate the idea of dancing around hitting blocks. It tires you out, but lifts the mood. The music is not something I would ever listen to outside of the game, but pumps me up when I'm playing and fits well with the beat. I started out sucking at it beyond measure, and I'm still terrible, but there is a genuine feeling of progression and improvement.

If you're playing solo, have a crack at beating me on the online leaderboard (it shouldn't be too hard), and there's a campaign to steadily increase the challenge as well. 

If you have a few friends around, Beat Saber is so fun that four of us spent New Years Eve embarrassing ourselves playing it, blaming failures on the steadily increasing amount of alcohol consumed. Hooking your PC up to a TV and playing on party mode is neat if you have friends over, allowing you to watch each other fail, laugh and save local scores in an easy and intuitive way. 

Yes, I do have video proof, but I probably won't share it. They'll kill me, which would be a dire start to 2020. Happy New Year everyone!

Just finally putting a review on this... I know it says I have 82.2 Hrs on record, however- I believe this is truly false as I have spent about 280+ Hours on SteamVR-- roughly half of that 280 hours was either spent playing Beatsaber, or spending enough time to set up Full Body Tracking(FBT)+Modding the game. I have just recently checked the store page and thought people would've been racking up hundreds of hours and thought mine was puny by comparison, but I also think that SteamVR is really just reducing the amount of hours each review actually says it has on the game. Also, as of this review- I have never hurt my wrists on any level, and you'll see why. But, here is my review- in milestones.

FIRST PURCHASE : Damn, I was so out of shape- I could barely play this game for 2 hours before having the realization that my left arm didnt want to extend over my head. I guess this is why people said "use the wrists" but I have felt the burn and loved it right after. From this point on, I only moved my entire arms while playing this, only ever "using my wrists" as an example to my friends when they were wondering why I dislike it.(Shown about 60 hours in-game logged time.) I still flail my arms around like a madman, and am pretty sure I fractured my thumb by slamming it into a wall and my thumb was between the wall and controller... but I still havent checked up on it with the doctor to this day because I have no idea how to explain how that happened.

1 Week Later : I only got to play this game 2 times in a whole week. That's how long it took for my arms to recover from the massive stress I put on the game. At this point, I wanted more. I havent exercised this much and I wanted more of it. It was addicting. I slapped that initial 2h gameplay (all done in 1 session with no breaks) and did 5 straight hours this time. Man, this was painful- but I loved this kind of pain. It was improvement. I had 2 major problems though.

1. I was using a Acer Headset. This is a forward tracking headset and lost vision of the wands whenever I moved them to my sides and quickly made me realize that I had to move my head with the movement of my wands. This caused some back problems that I had to deal with quickly. Don't use a Acer with this game.
2. I lived in a relatively small room with less than a 3x4 area to use as my "Play Area", but I wanted to love this experience as much as I could, and made meets end. This had to be changed for me to absolutely fall in love with this.

1 Month Later : From that play count of only 2 times a week, it was now up to 12 times at this point that I have played the game. The "Campaign" of this didnt exist when I played, so I was already done playing all the base maps and was getting quite bored of them. I turned to the modding discord for additional maps and ways to customize my game. I have probably started spending more time learning from tutorials how to convert a MMD Avatar to a .Avatar file for Beatsaber and recording that. I was able to consistently play each time for 4-6 hours non-stop. This was before Covid-19 and I hated going to a gym, so this was a way for me to ease my way into exercising more confidently. My arms started to tone up, but nothing super impressive, but I liked how they looked and wanted to continue this.

3 Months Later : I have to admit, I stopped playing the game more actively because I was spending a LOT of time getting Full Body Tracking working. I wasn't using a VIVE Pro at that point, it was a Acer headset and trying to mix the FBT to work with that. It was a long mess and I realized that I could only really enjoy playing this during winter time with my windows open, which caused some problems in the near future that caused me to stop playing for a while.

6 Months Later : Winter passed. I managed to log ~30 hours into the game at this point and was loving the community-made maps. They didn't exactly have a scale or good way of determining difficulty of each map, so it was a huge Hit-or-Miss scenario with each and every map I downloaded. So this was a slow time for me as I wanted to use maps to practice and get back into the zone of playing the game.
-This was when I learned that updates invalidate your mods and you need to constantly update them. At this point, I wish that the mods were permanent additions to the game.

1 Year Later : COVID-19 came. I almost have completely stopped playing the game due to various other reasons, one of which was just the sheer realization that I couldn't enjoy the game in the small space I had to play in. So I spent majority of this time working and getting enough money to finally move into a larger household, which indirectly also made me upgrade all of my hardware and desk space. I was finally playing games that I couldn't previously have played.

2 Years Later(Now) : I have by then upgraded my Acer headset to a VIVE Pro, moved into a larger place that also increased my Play Area to triple the size and finally be able to experience the game how it was meant to be. With mods from previous experiences as well. 50 more hours went into this game (more like 100 more...) and I can confidently say that me moving my entire arms every single time I have played, has improved my stamina. I constantly play this game without a shirt because I would just drench any shirt or towel I try putting on. I stream gameplay to my friends using mods to show them from a 3rd person view of me in FBT, trying to tell them how great this game is.

There is so many things that I have learned, earned, and now want to get because of this VR experience. I want to learn how to dance and play at the same time. I lost weight, made me gain confidence, and now... have put on some level of muscle, and that has drastically improved my mood for the better. I also want to finally be able to pick up streaming games because of this. I have gained more than the 30$ price tag is advertising. 

I also refuse to play the game using my wrists, so I will eventually meet the physical limitations of the speed of which I can swing my arms at. Also, do not play this way if you are in a house with many delicate objects around you, like siblings(20y/o+). I have swung at one of them so badly that they now are scared of VR.

Just to be clear, mods never went ANYWHERE, they were and always have been here. The devs have never removed them purposefully at any point in this games history.

My friends, mods will always be in Beat Saber (hopefully) and the devs will not "block" them. The reason there are none at the moment is that, new update -> new version -> mods OUTDATED, not "Gone". All experienced players know this is standard and we expect it at almost every update.  Modders from all over are most likely working hard updating said mods and will be out as soon as possible.

I highly doubt that the devs purposefully wanted to make just ONE of the new song packs paid. It is most likely for licensing purposes, to actually allow them to use the songs in the game.

Chill, play the OST a tad. And if you "need" your mods that badly, no harm in waiting a bit. However please don't assume they're gone.

Beat saber is a great game even without mods and I will continue to sink many hours into it alongside this great community.
